solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Last female deer succeeded initially in annual test

parts.note: a hind is a female red deer

indicators.note: one piece is placed within the other, as the clue says

parts.note: the MOT is the annual roadworthiness test for British cars

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the word succeeded is wanted

explanation.surface: A doe that was the very last to pass her yearly inspection.
explanation.walkthrough: The MOT is the yearly check British law requires for cars over three years old.
explanation.definitionFit: Hindmost means furthest back, so it is the one at the rear: last.

clue.text: Dissident woman's quote retracted

parts.note: her is the possessive for a woman, as in her book

indicators.note: drawn back, so the word cite is read backwards

parts.note: to quote is to cite

explanation.surface: A rebel woman takes back something she quoted.
explanation.definitionFit: A heretic holds views that depart from accepted doctrine, so a dissenter.

clue.text: Knight departs during broadcast's lowest point

parts.note: N is the chess notation for a knight

indicators.note: one thing happening within another, so a letter goes inside the word

parts.note: to broadcast is to air; the 's stands for is, joining it to the definition
D is the timetable abbreviation for departs

explanation.surface: A knight leaves partway through a broadcast, its worst moment.
explanation.definitionFit: The nadir is the point directly below the observer, hence the bottom or worst moment of anything.

clue.text: Film actor refurbished moorland barn

indicators.note: a refurbished building has been done over, so these letters are rebuilt into a new order

explanation.surface: A renovated barn out on the moors.
explanation.definitionFit: Marlon Brando was the American star of On the Waterfront and The Godfather.

clue.text: Rod's son cheers very loudly

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for son in family trees
ta is British slang for thanks, as is cheers
ff, fortissimo, is the musical marking for very loud

explanation.surface: A boy cheering at the top of his voice, with 's read as is.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain both 'cheers' and 'ta' are casual ways of saying thanks.
explanation.definitionFit: A staff is a long stick or pole carried in the hand.

clue.text: Handled soft fabric

definitions.meaning: past tense of feel: touched with the hands
a cloth made of matted, pressed wool

explanation.surface: Someone fingered a piece of soft cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: Felt is both the past tense of feel, to touch, and a pressed wool material.

clue.text: Green alder decaying below upset me

indicators.note: in a down clue the second piece sits under the first
in a down clue, upset turns the word me upside down
rotting wood falls apart, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A rotting alder tree that has upset the speaker.
explanation.definitionFit: Emerald is a bright green colour, named after the gemstone.

clue.text: Note the barking canines, for example

parts.note: te is the seventh note in tonic sol-fa

indicators.note: barking means mad, so these letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: Pay attention to the dogs that bark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'barking' scrambles THE into ETH. 'Canines' tempts toward dogs, but the definition means pointed teeth, an example of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Canines are the pointed teeth either side of the incisors, so examples of teeth.

clue.text: Body of policemen lean on pornographic business

parts.note: lean means thin
a blue film is a pornographic one
one's line is one's trade or business

explanation.surface: Police are leaning on a smut trade.
explanation.definitionFit: The thin blue line is a nickname for the police as the force keeping order.

clue.text: Jockey cleared the barrier finally

parts.note: to rid a place of something is to clear it

indicators.note: only the closing letters of the words the and barrier are wanted

explanation.surface: A jockey's horse jumped the last fence.
explanation.definitionFit: A jockey is someone who rides racehorses, a rider.

clue.text: A Greek character, the first woman to win

parts.note: chi is a letter of the Greek alphabet
Eve is the first woman in Genesis

explanation.surface: A Greek woman is the first to win something.
explanation.definitionFit: To achieve something, such as a goal, is to gain or win it.

clue.text: Run on to hill

indicators.note: in an across clue, a piece on another comes after it

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: An order to run up to the hill.
explanation.definitionFit: A tor is a rocky hilltop, especially on Dartmoor.

clue.text: German-born composer frequently heard another composer

indicators.note: the word is given as it sounds when spoken

parts.note: frequently means often, which many say with a silent T
J S Bach was a German composer

explanation.surface: One composer is often heard alongside a second.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heard' works on 'frequently' alone: OFTEN, said without its T, gives OFFEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Jacques Offenbach, born in Cologne, became famous for French operettas such as Orpheus in the Underworld.

clue.text: Plump freshwater fish in reserve

parts.note: the chub is a river fish of the carp family
something put by is kept in reserve

explanation.surface: A fat river fish kept in stock.
explanation.definitionFit: Chubby means pleasantly round and fat, like plump.

clue.text: Disconcert jogger heading off, vest half-exposed

indicators.note: the head, or first letter, of the word is removed

parts.note: a jogger is a runner

indicators.note: only half of the word vest is on show, its first part

explanation.surface: A jogger sets off with a vest that shows too much.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading off' takes the first letter from RUNNER, leaving UNNER; 'half-exposed' shows only the first half of VEST.
explanation.definitionFit: To unnerve someone is to shake their confidence, so to disconcert them.

clue.text: Left personal documents in German aircraft

indicators.note: these pieces are placed inside the other word

parts.note: ID is short for identity papers

explanation.surface: Someone left their papers in a German plane.
explanation.definitionFit: A glider is an engineless aircraft that rides air currents.

clue.text: Suspect ponders answer

indicators.note: used as an adjective, suspect means dodgy, so these letters are not to be trusted in their order

explanation.surface: A suspect thinks over how to reply.
explanation.definitionFit: To respond is to reply, to give an answer.

clue.text: Island's crime associated with crack or Ecstasy

parts.note: a sin is a wrongdoing
a crack is a gap
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: An island's crime problem is tied to crack cocaine and ecstasy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crack' and 'Ecstasy' suggest drugs; only Ecstasy is one here, crack is a gap.
explanation.definitionFit: Singapore is an island city-state off the tip of the Malay peninsula.

clue.text: Mum in studio regularly selected Oriental food

indicators.note: the quiet sign goes inside the picked letters
every other letter of the word studio is chosen

parts.note: mum as in keep mum means quiet, which is sh

explanation.surface: Mum, at a studio, regularly picks Japanese food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly selected' takes S, U, I from STUDIO; 'Mum' is silence, not a mother.
explanation.definitionFit: Sushi is a Japanese dish of vinegared rice with raw fish.

clue.text: Cockney's cry of distress encountering alien young bird

indicators.note: a Cockney speaker of London drops the H at the start of words

parts.note: a howl is a cry of pain or distress
ET is the alien of Spielberg's film

explanation.surface: A Londoner cries out on meeting an alien chick.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockneys, working-class Londoners, are said to drop their H, so HOWL loses it.
explanation.definitionFit: An owlet is a young owl, so a young bird.

clue.text: Father's dance step

definitions.meaning: pa is father, and ... is his, written without its apostrophe

explanation.surface: Dad's characteristic dance move.
explanation.definitionFit: Pas is the French ballet term for a step, as in pas de deux.

clue.text: Person cherished a large flower section

parts.note: a pet is a favourite, someone cherished
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: A loved one has a big flower.
explanation.definitionFit: A petal is one of the coloured leaves that together make up a bloom.

clue.text: Thin pastry split on the outside by uncultured learner

indicators.note: only the outermost letters of the word split are wanted

parts.note: rude can mean rough and unrefined
L is for learner, as on British L-plates

explanation.surface: A boorish trainee splits the pastry's outer layer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'split' looks like a verb acting on the pastry, but it is the word whose outer letters give ST.
explanation.definitionFit: Strudel is a central European dessert of fruit rolled in very thin layers of dough.

clue.text: Opening some port, Nigel reflected

indicators.note: seen as in a mirror, the letters read backwards
only part of the words port and Nigel is used

explanation.surface: Nigel thinks back on opening some port.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some' picks ORTNI from inside 'port, Nigel'; 'reflected' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: An intro is the opening section of a song or piece of writing.

clue.text: Plan central parts of kids' meal

indicators.note: only the middle letters of each word, kids' and meal, are used

explanation.surface: A scheme for the middle part of the children's dinner.
explanation.definitionFit: An idea can be a scheme or intention, so a plan.

clue.text: Abroad, Pete's acted as guide, describing some churches

indicators.note: abroad can mean all over the place, so these letters are scattered

parts.note: to guide someone is to lead them, past tense led

explanation.surface: Pete was a tour guide overseas, showing tourists churches.
explanation.definitionFit: A steepled church has a tall spire, so the word describes such buildings.
